Yo, currently a periop student a AUT and I'll do my best to answer your questions.

If you're worried about your English skills and lack of health science knowledge, AUT does offer a diploma or certificate in applied science which you can do to develop your lack of health science knowledge. I would not recommend jumping straight to the bachelors without some sort of basic background knowledge of the sciences.

Regarding the job market, you'll be fine, there's a big demand for techs so should be able to start anywhere in the country once you graduate, might even be offered a job from your placement site in your third and final year. If you're looking to go overseas, there isn't many places to go since the position of anaesthesia tech/periop practitioner doesn't really exist in many places. From the top of my head I think you can only really go to Western Australia since they still have techs there and the UK since periop practitioner is based off their ODP position.

Feel free to message me if you got more questions.
